newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends 43 cts higher in European cold snap.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends 43 cts higher in European cold snap.

text.p: IPE Brent futures ended higher on Thursday, catching up New York gains from New Year's eve and helped by a sustained spell of below-normal temperatures across Europe.
February Brent finished up 43 cents a barrel at $24.24 but was unable to maintain even larger gains after peaking early in the session at $24.61.
Dealers said the lack of a firm follow-up in New York, where contracts ended mixed, held Brent back in mundane afternoon trade.
Earlier January IPE gas oil ended $8.25 higher at $232 a tonne reflecting renewed demand for heating oil in a widespread European freeze.
Gas oil stretched its crack spread premium over Brent to $6 for February contracts.
Ice-jammed German waterways boosted gas oil barge premiums on northwest European markets.
With German consumers running on thinner stocks than in previous years some dealers are betting on substantial demand if the weather stays cold.
Weather forecasts were for continued below-normal temperatures at least until the weekend.
But NYMEX dealers were reluctant to follow London's lead citing milder than normal weather in the U.S. northeast heating oil market.
